- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.80) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to peak sentiment period.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: subtract 1–3% from forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.27) or volatile, model underestimates; add 1–4% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward mid-range.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings — filter out sentiment-driven outliers by averaging last 3–5 sentiment values before forecasting.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with 18-day moving average of historical prices if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” oscillations, model tends to overfit recent highs — apply a “sentiment dampening” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment has been above 0.75 for 3+ consecutive days.
